subject: Invoice window alignment: August ingestion timezone mismatch
messages:
From: Joshua Park <joshua.park@orchard.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@orchard.ai
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: [Orchard AI] August invoice looks off — ingestion window overlap?

Hi David,

We're reviewing the August invoice and noticed a large jump in ingest tokens for the Aug 27–31 window compared to previous weeks. Our internal logs show a small bump (around 12%), but the invoice suggests ~3.1x the expected token count for that period.

Suspect: our data pipeline switched to UTC timestamps on Aug 28 during a deploy, and that may have shifted event attribution across billing windows (your billing window is 00:00 PST). Can you confirm whether Redwood applies a fixed timezone for the ingestion window or uses the request timestamp as received?

Attached: orchard_usage_2026-08-27_to_2026-08-31.csv (sample rows), and our internal ingest header samples.

We need a quick reconciliation because this invoice is scheduled for payment on Sep 10 and the variance is material for our finance team. Can someone on your billing side trace ledger attribution and confirm whether this is a metering duplication or a timezone alignment issue?

Thanks — appreciate a timeline for the investigation.

Josh Park
Head of Platform Operations, Orchard AI
ops@orchard.ai

[attachment: orchard_usage_2026-08-27_to_2026-08-31.csv]

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Joshua Park <joshua.park@orchard.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Orchard AI] August invoice looks off — ingestion window overlap?

Hi Josh — thanks for the heads up and the sample CSV. I've opened a billing trace and copied Rafael (billing ops) and Grace (customer success) to help coordinate. Initial notes:

- Redwood's metering normalizes events to the tenant's configured timezone, which defaults to the account's billing timezone (PST) unless overridden. We also accept the request "sent_at" header when provided for attribution, but we fall back to server-received time when headers are missing or malformed.
- A 3.1x jump is larger than a simple TZ offset; we'll look for duplicated ingestion attempts, retry storms, or an accidental replay during your deploy window.

Can you confirm whether the records in your CSV have a "sent_at" header or if those timestamps are generated at ingestion? If you can forward a short sample of the raw request headers for a few rows (particularly around Aug 28 00:00–02:00 PST), that will speed up tracing.

I'll start a ledger-level dump for Aug 27–31 and run a delta against the per-request logs. Rafael, Grace — can you take point on the ledger export and engage infra if we see server-time duplicates?

Best,
David Kim
Billing Liaison, Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.ai

[attachment: redwood_billing-window-logs-aug.zip]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Joshua Park <joshua.park@orchard.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Orchard AI] August invoice looks off — ingestion window overlap?

Josh, David — I pulled the ledger export and basic reconciliation. Quick summary of findings so far:

- Ledger rows show two clusters of events for the Orchard tenant between 2026-08-28T06:55:00Z and 2026-08-28T07:12:00Z. The server-received timestamps are duplicated across a subset of request_ids (approx ~18k rows) while the client-sent timestamps in your CSV are unique.
- Evidence points to a replay at the HTTP layer: many events have identical bodies and only differ by a retry header our gateway injected. The gateway logs show a transient upstream 503 from one of your ingestion endpoints at 06:56Z, followed by aggressive client-side retries.
- Because our billing default is to use server-received time when the request contains no explicit idempotency key, those retried requests were attributed as separate events and billed.

Suggested short-term remediation:

1) We can grant a provisional credit for the duplicated server-received events pending a final audit.
2) Recommend enabling idempotency/request_id header on your client side (we have examples here: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/idempotency-guides).
3) Optionally switch your account's billing attribution to prefer client-sent timestamps (we can enable as a tenant-level toggle) — note this requires consistent sent_at header across retries.

Next steps: I propose we provisionally issue a credit for the duplicated token units (~18,364 rows) while we run a full 72-hour audit to confirm. Can you confirm whether Orchard wants credits applied to the Sep invoice or a proforma adjustment to the Aug invoice? Also please share the raw gateway logs for Aug 28 06:55–07:15Z UTC if possible.

Rafael Mendes
Head of Billing Operations, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai

[attachment: ledger_delta_sample_orchard_20260828.csv]

From: Joshua Park <joshua.park@orchard.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Orchard AI] August invoice looks off — ingestion window overlap?

Thanks Rafael — that aligns with what we were starting to suspect. A few quick answers: 

- Our client does not currently set an idempotency/request_id header for batch uploads; retries are exponential and driven from the HA proxy layer.
- We can provide the gateway logs for the 06:55–07:15Z window (sending compressed logs now to the Drive link you shared).
- Orchard would prefer a credit applied to the Aug invoice if the audit confirms duplication; finance wants the Sep payment to proceed on schedule with any credit showing as an adjustment rather than deferring the full invoice.

Action items from Orchard:
- I'll upload the gateway logs and a few raw HTTP samples to the Drive folder in the next hour.
- We'll add idempotency headers in our next release (ETA Sep 10).

Thanks for the fast triage — Grace, please flag if Redwood needs an official acceptance form for the credit so our AP team can reconcile.

Josh
Head of Platform Operations, Orchard AI
